16:About fifteen systems change state blocks inside kernel write scopes, and a dozen presentation subscribers must learn which parts changed without the kernel ever handing out state or depending on the scene tree. This ADR fixes the whole path: a kernel-owned observer registry (not engine signals) delivering `(block, tick, keys, events)` batches to five subscriber classes through a class-bound `NotifyFacet` issued only to the composition root, 64-bit integer dirty keys `(KIND << 32) | id` collected allocation-free in the write scope with collapse to `ALL` at a latched cap, a per-frame merge for presentation classes (sorted again at frame end), one `ALL` delivery after every load, and an aud
81:  P0  latch MAX_DIRTY_KEYS knob (a change made during tick T-1 takes effect now): set_cap(k) on every tick and frame KeyBuf
143:5. The registry holds fewer than `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS` (96).
151:- **Deferred application replaces the per-tick list copy.** CR-10 says P5 iterates a snapshot of the subscriber list taken before P5. Copying a list every tick would allocate. The kernel instead queues `subscribe`, `unsubscribe` and prune requests and applies them at the start of each delivery boundary (before the per-tick delivery of a tick and before the frame-end delivery), rebuilding the per-block subscriber arrays only when a request is pending. **The rebuild allocates nothing:** the subscription table is a fixed array of `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS` slots, each per-block subscriber list is a fixed-capacity `PackedInt32Array` of slot indices (capacity `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, with a count) rebui
207:**`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`** (kernel knob, 256, range 32 to 4096, at least 128 while `graph.state` is registered). Buffers are **allocated** at the sized capacity `buf.size()` fixed at the registry freeze (the knob value then) and never resized. The **active collapse threshold** is a separate field, `KeyBuf.cap`. The knob may be **lowered** at run time: at the next tick's P0 the kernel latches the new value and calls `set_cap(k)` on every tick and every frame `KeyBuf` (a change during P2 of `T` uses the old value in `T`'s P5, KRN AC); raising it above the sized capacity is refused with the existing `KNOB_REFUSED` violation. `set_cap` is allocation-free; if a frame buffer already holds more than 
217:var cap: int                                     # active collapse threshold, 1 .. buf.size(); set by set_cap at the P0 latch
258:- **Exactness.** Capacity is the latched cap (the knob value, 256 by default), so exactly `cap` distinct keys are listed and the next distinct key gives `ALL`; a key marked 1,000 times is one key (probed 2026-10-28, `EXACT256`: `is_all` false, count 256; `OVERFLOW` at 257: `is_all` true).
298:It uses `KeyBuf` (`src/kernel/facets/key_buf.gd`) and allocates nothing after `_init`. **Its capacity is the sized capacity, not the latched cap.** A lowered knob makes the kernel collapse earlier; an accumulator that collapses later never loses a key (it holds a finer set that is a subset of what a full re-read covers, and any `is_all` batch still propagates), so keeping the sized capacity is safe and avoids a kernel-core edge from a presentation-side type. The cost is only that the accumulator can be finer than the kernel; the knob-lowering test (Validation Criteria) covers the kernel side.
318:- `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty` (open block required; discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE`, `CLOSED`). **The limits are global, not per block:** `MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK` (64) across all blocks in one tick, and `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` x 64 across all blocks in one frame; overflow drops the newest and counts `EVENT_OVERFLOW`.
327:**P5, per tick.** The kernel applies deferred subscription changes, then for each dirty block in ascending index and each `PER_TICK` subscription of that block in subscription order, arms the shared `NotifyContext`, calls the handler with the block's tick batch, checks the returned token (identity and epoch, ADR-0003 § 3), and records `INCOMPLETE` or `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER` as needed. Then each tick buffer is folded into its frame buffer: if the frame buffer is empty the two `KeyBuf` objects are swapped (O(1); the swapped-in buffer was closed at P4, so it is already sorted); otherwise `frame_buf.union_from(tick_buf)` runs (a `has()` union, a union beyond the latched cap sets `is_all`) and the
354:- **Cadence.** In unit, integration and CI soak tests with small worlds the sweep runs **every tick** (`AUDIT_EVERY_TICK`); under `STRICT_DEBUG` it runs at the tripwire's `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` (60) and within `TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` (1.0), so there it is a sample, not a proof. A bool guards the whole path; release exports pay one branch per tick.
422:- **Must** give every mutator a unit test that runs it in a fresh kernel fixture and asserts the exact keys it marks (the fixture subscribes a `RecordingSubscriber` and compares the batch); **must** keep `AUDIT_EVERY_TICK` on in every integration and soak test.
515:- **The subscription list rebuild is slow with many pending requests.** Mitigation: rebuild only on a pending request, at most `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS` 96 entries; none in steady state.
521:- **A lowered `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` has no effect.** Mitigation: the active cap is a field separate from the allocated capacity and is latched into every buffer at P0 (§ 3, § 4); the validation case lowers it and checks the collapse point.
## Tuning Knobs

All knobs below are **provisional until the kernel spike**. Every knob traces to a Section D symbol. "Tunability": **set-once** = fixed at project start, changing it is a code/data migration; **boot** = registration data frozen at `BOOTING → LOADING`, changeable between runs; **runtime** = may be changed by a dev console between ticks (honoured at P6) without invalidating any stored value.

content.content: 60	**CR-1a. Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads that reach the simulation (H9); which files may read a clock at all is the allow-list owned by ADR-0010 `SIM-02`, not kept here *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*. **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16); (6) `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()`, the unconditional last step of the driver frame: `TickDriver.frame()` is a two-statement wrapper, `_frame_body(delta_us)` (steps 1 to 5, which may return early on a pause, a restore request, a fault or a zero-tick frame) and then `deliver_frame_end()`, with no statement after it, so no exit path skips frame-end delivery (ADR-0001 section 1, test KRN-FRAME-END) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*. **The accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** (from `LOADING`, `PAUSED` or `SAVING`), so a load, an autosave or a pause never produces catch-up ticks afterwards. The driver node has a process priority that runs it before the presentation nodes, so presentation reads the tick the driver just produced. **Step 0 — input sample, and the priority table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: nothing in the driver's step list sampled input, so the best-case latency of D.4 rested on an unstated ordering. The order inside one rendered frame is now fixed by process priority (lower runs first): **(0)** the input adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE` object; it reads the engine's input state for this frame and calls `submit`, so its commands are admitted before the boundary service and the tick loop); **(1)** the `TickDriver` node (boundary service, then the tick loop, then forgiveness, result flush, paused service, then `deliver_frame_end()`); **(1.5)** the host-service slot (`HOST_SERVICE`, `SaveHost` only: its per-frame poll runs after the driver and observes the last committed tick boundary; ADR-0006); **(2)** presentation (the single presentation host and its stages: Pixel-Perfect pipeline, HUD, Lighting, Audio), which read what the driver just committed.
